sources.title: Nikon: Long exposures of moving water — Tony Sweet
Canon: Getting started with landscape photography

claims.text: Nikon describes tripod stabilization and remote release or camera delay. Its photographer first meters a normal exposure with chosen ISO and aperture, then adjusts duration for an ND filter. Waterfall examples include dim-light exposures without ND and a five-stop ND exposure lasting 25 seconds.
Canon describes ND filters for longer waterfall exposures in brighter light. Its three-stop example changes one-eighth second to one second at unchanged ISO and aperture.

candidates.name: Use available dim light for moving water
candidates.reason: Stabilize the camera, meter a correctly exposed baseline and compare several durations for water texture. Start with available light when it permits the intended duration.
limitations: No universal best shutter speed follows from the examples. Flow, desired texture, light and camera controls differ; publication date is unstated.

candidates.name: Add neutral density when light limits exposure duration
candidates.reason: Establish a baseline first. Add ND when available light prevents the desired duration at the chosen ISO and aperture; adjust exposure for its actual stop reduction.
limitations: A filter is conditional rather than a required purchase. Manufacturer examples do not establish a particular product advantage or the best result for a scene.
